target_customer: Democratic and progressive campaigns, advocacy groups and later large brands that buy paid media and want to know which creative persuades
problem: Campaigns and brands spend heavily on ads and messages without knowing which versions actually change opinions. Swayable runs randomized controlled trials on online panels to measure persuasion before and during spend.
business_model: B2B SaaS and research services, per test or per contract
product_category: Message and creative testing, persuasion measurement

founders.name: James Slezak
prior_employers: The New York Times (Executive Director of Digital Strategy)
founders.background_notes: From the YC company page. The Feb 2018 TechCrunch profile says Swayable was founded by three former physicists but does not name the other two, so they are not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard web stack plus experiment design: recruiting panels from sources such as Fiverr and Mechanical Turk, randomizing exposure and estimating persuasion effects. The hard part was statistical rigor and panel quality, not infrastructure.

defensibility.rationale: Method of randomized message testing was reproducible by data shops. A growing archive of experiments gave some data advantage, and the founders published academic work, but the product itself was copyable.

incumbents: large polling and market research firms
takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not established from dated sources. Civis later marketed a Creative Focus tool using randomized trials, but the date of that launch was not found.

market_need_then: Democratic groups were investing in campaign tech after 2016. Higher Ground Labs funded a 13 company cohort in April 2018 and TechCrunch in Feb 2018 described demand for evidence on which political messages persuade.

branding.domain_note: Company site moved from swayable.com to www.swayable.com. No domain purchase story found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Evidence based, research led (own insights blog publishes test findings)

brand_strength.rationale: Known inside political tech and academic circles through Higher Ground Labs and a 2024 peer reviewed study, but no sources show consumer visibility or brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Swayable appears to be a durable niche company. It started with progressive campaigns after 2016, expanded to brands, and is still listed as active with about 30 people. Its edge was scientific credibility from a physicist founder and published experiment work. Public funding is thin, so growth may have been revenue funded, and no outcome search found layoffs, an exit or a shutdown.
notes: The company website was fetched via redirect notice only (swayable.com redirects to www.swayable.com), content not read. Competitor list left empty because Civis Analytics and Grow Progress pages found had no date near the batch. Unverified aggregator claims: CB Insights lists $120K over 3 rounds with a seed on 2018-04-01, Seedtable lists a March 2018 seed with A-Level Capital, and New Media Ventures announced $1.2M across 13 startups including Swayable. An Advertising Week bio mentions Sequoia and YC as backers, not confirmed elsewhere. The $100K amount is the typical Higher Ground Labs investment per cohort, not a Swayable specific figure confirmed by name.
